title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of a 1984 letter, in English, to a specialist in hyperbolic geometry; the recipient is unknown. It belongs to Grothendieck's programme of 'surgery of conformal surfaces'.

Setting (previous page):
- X is a compact Riemann surface with boundary of hyperbolic type, with boundary components indexed by I.
- It is canonically capped to a closed surface X^ with marked points s_i. Each hole is filled by a conformal disc D_i; the system (D_i) is called 'admissible'.
- Plausibly the gluing uses the hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary: arc-length parametrisation of each boundary geodesic, then gluing in the unit disc. Rotations are absorbed, so the capping is canonical. The precise definition of 'admissible' is on earlier pages.
- Each pointed disc (D_i, s_i) determines a conformal radius, i.e. a hermitian norm on T_{s_i}X^. This gives r = (r_i) in a product of R^{+*}-torsors.
- Grothendieck expects the radii to determine the discs, with the admissible radii cut out by r_i < rho_i.
- The key case is the pair of pants. Then X^ is the Riemann sphere Sigma, with s_i = 0, 1, infinity, and one must classify admissible triples of discs.

The model:
- Put a round metric on Sigma, conjugated by a Mobius map so that 0, 1, infinity are equally spaced on the equator, which is the real projective line.
- Cut Sigma into three 120-degree lunes ('orange slices') Q_i, centred at s_i. Their boundaries are three half great circles C_i meeting at the poles P+ and P-. These poles are the fixed points of the order-3 Mobius maps permuting 0, 1, infinity, i.e. e^{+-i pi/3}.
- Each Q_i is a simply connected conformal disc pointed at s_i. Through its Riemann map to the unit disc one forms the concentric subdiscs lambda_i Q_i, with 0 < lambda_i < 1.
- Conjecture: the admissible systems are exactly the triples (lambda_0 Q_0, lambda_1 Q_1, lambda_inf Q_inf). Allowing lambda_i = 0 gives degenerate discs, i.e. cusps.

Consequences Grothendieck draws:
- The pants, embedded in the sphere, would be totally ordered along each coordinate.
- Their common intersection would be the theta graph formed by the C_i and P+-.
- This would supply new intrinsic objects attached to every pair of pants (P+-, C_i) and new parameters lambda_i.
- One must then relate lambda_i to Thurston's boundary lengths l_i. He doubts that l_i depends on lambda_i alone.
- His earlier idea of fibering the bordered-surface Teichmuller space MB~ over the pointed-surface Teichmuller space M~ via Fenchel-Nielsen data is therefore non-intrinsic.
- He proposes instead the canonical description MB~ = M~ x [0,1[^I, via the capping map, with r_i = lambda_i rho_i.
- The dimension count is consistent: 6g-6+3n = (6g-6+2n) + n.

He asks:
- whether the model holds;
- how the hyperbolic metric changes when a collar is removed (next page);
- for an explicit formula of the pant metric in terms of the lambda_i.
errors: The lune model is almost certainly false as stated. It forces disc D_0 to range over a one-parameter nested family depending only on lambda_0, while the true capping disc D_0 depends on all three boundary lengths (l_0, l_1, l_inf). Example: with l_0 fixed, varying l_1 and l_inf changes the conformal radius and shape of D_0 in the sphere normalised at 0, 1, infinity.

The predicted common intersection of all pants (the fixed theta graph with vertices P+-) is also implausible. As boundary lengths go to infinity, hyperbolic pants degenerate (heuristically, after capping) to the critical graph of the Jenkins-Strebel quadratic differential with residues proportional to (l_0, l_1, l_inf). That graph is the theta graph through e^{+-i pi/3} only for equal lengths. Otherwise its vertices move, and when one length exceeds the sum of the other two it becomes a figure-eight/dumbbell graph. So the union of the discs D_i over all pants should not stay inside the lunes Q_i.

The 'expectation' on the previous page (radii determine discs; admissibility iff r_i < rho_i with fixed rho_i) inherits the same problem. Grothendieck himself notes there that it conflicts with his earlier expectation of a natural operation on MB~.
The description MB~ = M~ x [0,1[^I is fine as a topological statement: MB~ is a product with lengths in R_{>0}^I, and cells are homeomorphic. Its claimed canonical content depends on the false model.

ideas.what: Canonical capping of a bordered hyperbolic surface. Glue discs along the arc-length parametrised geodesic boundary to get a closed pointed Riemann surface, viewed as a canonical map MB~ -> M~ with fibres parametrised by the disc data.
ideas.modern_name: Capping/filling map from Teichmuller space of bordered surfaces to that of punctured surfaces; Riemann surfaces with parametrised boundary (Segal's gluing category)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fenchel-Nielsen and Thurston for the length coordinates; Segal (c. 1987) and Huang for gluing Riemann surfaces with parametrised boundaries
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmuller tower and surgery of surfaces in general terms; I am unsure whether the specific capping construction appears there.

ideas.what: Conformal radius at s_i as a point of an R^{+*}-torsor (hermitian norm on the tangent space), used as a coordinate on disc systems.
ideas.modern_name: Conformal radius / capacity; tangent-vector data on M_{g,n} (e.g. psi-class circle bundles)

ideas.what: Orange-slice decomposition of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}: three lunes bounded by half great circles meeting at the two fixed points e^{+-i pi/3} of the S_3 symmetry. Proposed as intrinsic geometry attached to every pair of pants.
ideas.modern_name: The 'clean' theta graph dessin on P^1 / critical graph of the symmetric Jenkins-Strebel differential
ideas.usually_credited_to: Strebel for quadratic differentials; Grothendieck (Esquisse) for dessins; later Kontsevich, Penner, Mulase-Penkava for the ribbon-graph/Strebel link

ideas.what: Conjecture that admissible disc triples are exactly concentric subdiscs lambda_i Q_i of the lunes, giving new pant parameters lambda_i in [0,1[.
Question of comparing the hyperbolic metrics of X and X' when a collar is removed; explicit pant metric in terms of the parameters.
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity/comparison of hyperbolic metrics under inclusion (Schwarz-Pick type) for bordered surfaces with geodesic boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: partial classical results (Schwarz-Pick, collar lemma: Keen, Buser)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's sought-for 'intrinsic' graph inside every pair of pants is the critical graph of the symmetric Jenkins-Strebel differential, the clean theta dessin with vertices e^{+-i pi/3}. Implicitly he links the conformal capping of hyperbolic pants to Strebel graphs and dessins. The later large-boundary-length theory (hyperbolic surfaces degenerating to metric ribbon graphs: Bowditch-Epstein, Mondello, Do) gives the correct version, in which the graph moves with the length ratios. Whether the conformal discs of canonical capping converge to the Strebel picture is a natural and, I believe, not fully written-up question.
missed.quote: The intersection of all would be this system of three half circles C_i , and the two poles P+,P- would play a significant role in the geometry of the pants
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It ties Grothendieck's surgery programme to the ribbon-graph cell decomposition of moduli space. It also yields a concrete question: describe the asymptotics of capping discs D_i(l) as l -> infinity in terms of Strebel graphs.

missed.claim: Explicit description of the canonical capping map MB~ -> M~ for pants: the three discs D_i(l_0, l_1, l_inf) in P^1, their conformal radii, and an explicit hyperbolic metric of a pant in sphere coordinates. As far as I know this has no closed-form treatment.
missed.quote: the basic problem of relying pants to spherical geometry, and more specifically, whether the model above is likely to hold, or is definitely false
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Conformal radii of capping discs relate to Liouville/Takhtajan-Zograf-type action functionals and psi-class constructions. An explicit pant formula would be a useful special-function result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting unpublished conjecture: a concrete, though almost certainly false, lune model for canonically capped pants. Its implicit theta graph and fixed poles foreshadow the Strebel/ribbon-graph picture. Nothing here is a finished result missed by the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'relying pants to spherical geometry' is Grothendieck's typo for 'relating'; the image confirms 'relying'.
The struck-out word before 'half circles' is a typo for 'three' ('thwee', overtyped), not part of the text.
A dash in the left margin before 'discs λ_i Q_i' marks a typed correction; the over-typed 'discs' at the end of the previous line is struck out.
The handwritten archive folio number at the bottom left may read '13' rather than '19'; the typed page number is 5.
